newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Senate hikes penalties for drug lords.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Senate hikes penalties for drug lords.

text.p: Colombia's Senate approved legislation on Tuesday raising prison sentences for drug trafficking to a maximum of 60 years from a current maximum of just 24 years.
Government officials have said the legislation could help Colombia avoid a new blacklisting by the United States for its perceived failure to act aggressively enough in the war on drugs.

The new sentencing law, which must still be approved by the lower house of Congress, establishes a minimum jail sentence of 20 years for drug trafficking and a maximum of 60 years. It comes too late for Colombia's most notorious drug lords, however.

Brothers Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, the billionaire leaders of the Cali drug mob, were sentenced to very light sentences in January that could see them walk free in as little as five years.

That decision, handed down by a judge in the southwest city of Cali which the Rodriguezes once ran as their personal fiefdom, sparked a public uproar in Washington and fuelled widespread speculation that Colombia will be "decertified" again on Feb. 27, when President Bill Clinton will announce whether the country is a trustworthy ally in the anti-drug fight.
Decertification for a second consecutive year could prompt punitive U.S. commercial sanctions that Clinton fell short of impiosng last year.
